snippet.description:
👉 Xiegu G7250: https://go.temporarilyoffline.com/4s9z39
Use Code "TO15" for $15 off!
❤️ Get My Free Newsletter: https://temporarilyoffline.com/pages/newsletter-signup

The Xiegu G7250 is real, powered on, and operating. In this video, I’m sharing the first real-world video and audio footage I’ve seen of Xiegu’s upcoming 100-watt HF and 6-meter SDR transceiver, rather than computer renderings of product images. We’ll examine the actual G7250 hardware, its separate RF deck and 7-inch touchscreen control head, the D-Core direct RF-sampling system, spectrum display, waterfall, physical controls, microphone, and what the radio sounds like in operation.

The Xiegu G7250 is currently described as a split-design software-defined radio covering 0.5–30 MHz and 50–54 MHz, with up to 100 watts on HF and 90 watts on 6 meters. Announced operating modes include SSB, CW, AM, NFM, and digital modes. Other preliminary features include adjustable DSP filters, noise reduction, noise blanking, voice recording, CW message memories, network-based baseband streaming, and a built-in automatic antenna tuner with a stated 20–150 ohm matching range. Xiegu is also advertising a receiver MDS of -138 dBm, a maximum transmit current of 25 amps, and a 1 Hz minimum tuning step. These specifications are still preliminary and could change before production.

One of the biggest unanswered questions is the connection between the G7250 control head and RF deck. Xiegu’s promotional information describes Ethernet and network functionality, but it has not yet been confirmed whether the control head can operate through a normal network switch, router, VPN, or internet connection, or whether it is limited to a direct local cable. Pricing has also not been announced. A European distributor currently lists a preliminary September 30, 2026 release date, but that date is not yet a firm worldwide shipping commitment.

This video covers everything currently known about the Xiegu G7250, including the first operating footage, D-Core architecture, receiver demonstrations, preliminary specifications, release-date information, Ethernet questions, antenna-tuner limitations, and how this new 100-watt Xiegu compares with radios such as the Xiegu G90, X6200

In This weeks Radio Dork news:
In the spirit of maintaining emergency communications and making friends, an amateur radio operator group is building a new videoconferencing community that uses the internet instead of radio waves to talk with strangers around the world.
As reported by the Amateur Radio Daily website, the new online-only video group for licensed ham radio operators worldwide and is intended to support and build face-to-face friendships.
For more information about this new 24/7 online video-conferencing group and how to join, contact Murray, K3BEQ or Roger, KE8LCM.

Radio authorities in Japan have reported multiple enforcement actions throughout the months of June and July, including warnings, fines and administrative suspensions for unlicensed amateur radio installations aboard ships and in vehicles. 
As reported by the hamlife.jp website, one of those caught up in the sting was a 52 year old resident of Sishiwa city who was subsequently sentenced to 42 months of administrative suspension for illegally operating a two-way radio in his vehicle, a violation of Article 4 of the Radio Act of Japan.

On July 14 broadcasters from over 30 states lobbied on Capitol Hill in Washington DC to advance the "AM Radio for Every Vehicle" Act, amid concerns over vehicle manufacturers planning to no longer include AM radios in new vehicles, due to interference from electric vehicles. 
As reported by insideradio.com, Curtis LeGey, President and CEO of the National Association of Broadcasters believes that keeping AM radios in the dashboard of all cars is exceedingly important, and that if AM radios are not included in automobiles it would cause harm to consumers.

A Kentucky family has filed a civil lawsuit against their county school board and the sheriff department, alleging that in January of 2025, an off-duty sheriff’s deputy seized the amateur radio equipment of a licensed high school student after reports that the student was transmitting on a public, non-law enforcement frequency that his amateur radio license authorized him to use.
The 51 page lawsuit goes on to allege that the unidentified student's civil rights were further violated when the school further retaliated by suspending him from class and having is father arrested when he tried to intervene with the equipment seizures.
All charges were later dropped by the county district court after ruling that the seizure of the equipment without a warrant was illegal and inadmissible in court, resulting in the sheriff's deputy that carried-out the seizure being suspended from the Sherrif's department.
The lawsuit claims that the student, identified only as L.B. was also suspended three times despite the school principal confirming that no rules had been violated.
The family is seeking damages and an order blocking the district from enforcing a radio policy that it claims has been improperly adopted.

And now for the FCC enforcement roundup. Here is the breakdown of what the FCC got up to in the month of July, 2026.
The FCC proposed multiple fines and reached settlement agreements with over a dozen wireless phone service providers,
and they proposed a $40,000 dollar fine for a Connecticut man accused of operating a pirate radio station on a commercial FM frequency.
And the part you've all been waiting for: the total number of arrests, fines or jail-time for CB radio, GMRS, and Amateur radio operators was... ZERO. 

And that is all of the radio-dork news that is fit to print. Join me again next week, or sooner, when I may, or may not, do this again. Good night,  and good luck

snippet.title: Compact HF Antenna.  Is it a dipole or is it a vertical? Great for high angle radiation.
snippet.description:
This is an interesting antenna designed by Peter G3OJV. It was originally developed as a vertical antenna to provide high-angle radiation, making it well suited for shorter daytime skip contacts.

However, if you look at its construction, you could also argue that it is essentially a dipole folded into half the length. This compact design allows it to fit comfortably into smaller gardens or backyards, while its very low profile makes it an excellent choice for stealth installations.

Whichever way you choose to classify it, this is a fascinating antenna 
that is well worth experimenting with—and, above all, great fun to build and use!

snippet.title: I Took an 800-Watt Ham Radio Station to a Pub!
snippet.description:
I packed a DX Commander Expedition and an entire high-power portable HF station into two large Peli cases and took it to Telford Amateur Radio Club for an evening in the field.

The station comprised my Kenwood TS-590SG, Tokyo Hy-Power HL-700B amplifier, lithium batteries, laptop, iPad second monitor and a DX Commander Expedition with 32 x 7-ft / 2m radials mounted in a water-filled patio umbrella base.

Once the club members had helped (watched!) me assemble everything, we were on the air within 20-minutes. What began as a demonstration quickly became a proper pile-up, with contacts across 40m, 20m, 15m and 10m - and we were even spotted on 6m.

Despite quite a high local noise level, around 100 stations went into the log during approximately 90 minutes of operating. Great signals, lovely evening light and tremendous fun.

Many thanks to everyone at Telford Amateur Radio Club for the welcome, help, coffee and excellent buffet - and thanks to everyone who called me, including the following who made it into the video:

G3HRO, PD9PWR, G4IRN, PA3MIR, F4LQP, M0JSX, OH2GBA, HB9HWS, PD1AR, PD3RL, LA6AY, M7HCV, SP2NW, G1IBS - and many more!

Apologies if I have copied any callsign incorrectly from the recording!

73, Callum M0XXT

snippet.title: İnanılmaz Hassasiyet! Bu radyo çok  uzak FM radyoları dinliyor. Yeni nesil oto  çipli FM Radyolar
snippet.description:
Bugün sizlerle yeni nesil oto çipli FM radyo alıcılarını inceleyeceğiz. Günümüzdeki en hassas  FM radyo alıcılarını genelde bu oto çipli radyolar oluşturmaktadır. Cihazın kalbinde, normalde lüks otomobillerin multimedya sistemlerinde kullanılan NXP TEF6686 çipi yer alır. Bu çip sayesinde cihaz, standart taşınabilir radyoların asla duyamayacağı uzak mesafe (DX) FM sinyallerini inanılmaz bir hassasiyetle yakalar. PACS (Frekans Bant Genişliği Optimizasyonu): Yan yana binen iki istasyonu birbirinden tereyağından kıl çeker gibi ayırır.Bu da Şehir içi çekimlerde veya güçlü istasyonların hemen yanındaki zayıf sinyalleri yakalamamızı sağlar. iMS & EMS: Çoklu yansıma (Multipath) parazitlerini ve şehir içi gürültülerini minimuma indirir. Standart 87.5-108 MHz dışında, 64-108 MHz (OIRT dahil) genişletilmiş FM bandını destekler. Ayrıca FM modunda 12'den fazla farklı filtre bant genişliği seçeneği sunar

snippet.title: CLARA SOTA Activation of South Monarch Ridge, August 3, 2026!
snippet.description:
#fitness #hiking #hikingadventures #sota #summitsontheair #hamradio #hamradiooperator #parksontheair #colorado mountains #morsecodehamster 
Please subscribe to my channel for more adventures! [and do forgive the audio lapse near the end while Mike is on his hand-held walking down the hill...I do my best!] 
The following details of this event are supplied by Bob Witte, K0NR, CLARA President:

These folks have indicated they will participate in the CLARA SOTA event on Saturday.

Bob K0NR
Joyce K0JJW
Dick K0RWE
Doug K0ILO plus one
Mike KE0PWR plus one (Laurel)
Walt W0CP
Sam W5CU

Many of you are experienced with SOTA activating, so you can just operate as usual.
There are two things to pay attention to with so many activators on the summit:

1. Two meter band:  there will be a lot of activity on this band, with many Colorado S2S opportunities. For the most part, we need to have only one station transmitting on the band at a time to avoid interference. Let's coordinate among ourselves to make this happen. 

One possible exception: we may be able to operate SSB or CW on the lower portion of the band at the same time another station is operating FM in the upper portion. We did this on Mount Blue Sky today with some minor interference. I think only Mike, Joyce and I have 2m SSB/CW, so let's coordinate.

2. HF Bands: The HF situation is similar, but there are more bands to choose from. If you are operating HF coordinate with the other activators so that only one station is transmitting on a band.

On the Saturday of the event (Aug 1), Bob/K0NR and Joyce/K0JJW will be doing a SOTA activation from South Monarch Ridge (also known as the Monarch Crest), right above Monarch Pass. See https://sotl.as/summits/W0C/SP-058
Everyone is invited to join in. If you’ve never done a SOTA activation before, this is your
chance! Bring your own gear or use ours. Or just ride along and enjoy the view from the top.
If you are experienced with SOTA, we would love to have you along, too!

snippet.title: Writs of Assistance & ALPRs: Why Traffic Cameras Are Modern General Warrants
snippet.description:
In 1761, British writs of assistance gave officials blanket authorization to search anyone, anywhere, at any time—a major catalyst for the American Revolution and the drafting of the Fourth Amendment.

​Fast forward to today: Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs) scan millions of drivers daily, logging location, time, and direction of travel without suspicion or a judicial warrant. Over 99% of those scanned aren't suspected of any crime. Instead of needing probable cause to search, the system searches everyone and looks for reasons later.

​Texas citizens don't have to accept mass warrantless dragnet tracking.

​🏛️ TAKE ACTION NOW:

Submit an official public comment to the Texas House Committee on Delivery of Government Efficiency (DOGE) before their official hearing.

​👉 Submit Comment Here: https://waller209.com/819

(⚠️ Make sure to select "Data Privacy and Security" from the dropdown menu!)

​Key Talking Points to Include in Your Comment:

​Require Warrants for Location History: Mandate judicial warrants based on probable cause before law enforcement or vendors can query or retain historical location records.

​Close the TDPSA Loophole & End Subsidies: Hold public-sector surveillance vendors to the same consumer data privacy standards applied under the Texas Data Privacy and Security Act, and stop using taxpayer funds and public rights-of-way to subsidize warrantless networks.

​Subscribe to stay tuned for Part 2!

Welcome to the live stream of Pune HAMs and Amateur Radio Club (VU2PHQ) @punehams !!! 🎙️📻

Join us as we sit down with Mr. Dhirendra Singh Kholia (VU3CER) "Dhiru" to explore the intersection of software engineering, Linux roots, and homebrew RF. From custom transceivers and APRS/Meshtastic nodes to circuit design and debugging, this episode covers the complete journey of a modern amateur radio tinkerer. 

Whether you're looking for beginner-friendly projects, advice on setting up your first workbench, or insight into open-source RF design, tune in and join the conversation!

• The Spark & Software Roots
  - Discovering amateur radio and transitioning from Linux/software into RF engineering.

• Homebrewing & Technical Exploration
  - What "homebrewing" truly means on the workbench.
  - Deep-dive into favorite builds: Amplifiers, digital transceivers, APRS, and Meshtastic nodes.
  - End-to-end design workflow: Ideas, KiCad schematics, PCB design, and RF debugging tactics.
  - Fusing IoT devices with traditional radio and the power of open-source documentation.

• Advice for Aspiring & Senior Homebrewers
  - How to start building at any age (from young engineers to 40s, 50s, and beyond).
  - High-confidence beginner projects & avoiding common beginner pitfalls.
  - Minimum budget toolsets needed to build safely and effectively.

• Learning Resources & Reference Material
  - Top books, blogs, courses, and online communities shaping modern homebrewers.

snippet.title: Hunting New POTA Parks Just Got Easier — Meet ParkWatch!
snippet.description:
Many of you already know how much I enjoy hunting new Parks On The Air, World Wide Flora & Fauna, Lakes and Lagoons On The Air, and Islands On The Air references.

Download ParkWatch from my QRZ page - https://www.qrz.com/db/VE9CF

For me, portable ham radio is about much more than simply putting another contact in the log. I enjoy chasing new parks, adding new DXCC entities, following favourite activators, and discovering portable stations from around the world.

One of my biggest frustrations has been finding software that works the way I want it to. POTAPlus has seen very little development over the past several years, while many other ham radio applications remain available only for Windows.

As a Mac user, I wanted something modern, flexible, and easy to use through Google Chrome. Rather than continuing to wait for someone else to build it, I decided to take the bull by the horns and create my own solution.

That summer project became ParkWatch.

ParkWatch is a Google Chrome-based application designed for park hunters and portable radio chasers. It works with several popular operating programs, including POTA, WWFF, LLOTA, and IOTA.

The goal is simple: help operators focus on the contacts that matter most to them.

That might mean hunting a new park reference, finding a new DXCC entity, following a favourite activator, watching a particular band or mode, or working toward a personal portable radio goal.

Instead of searching through several different spotting services and scrolling through large numbers of contacts, ParkWatch brings portable radio activity together in one place and helps hunters concentrate on what they still need.

ParkWatch is constantly being developed. New ideas are being tested, existing features are being improved, and I am always looking for better ways to make POTA, WWFF, IOTA, LLOTA, and other portable ham radio programs more enjoyable.

This project started as a tool for my own operating, but it has grown into something I hope can help other amateur radio operators enjoy park hunting and portable radio even more.

ParkWatch is still beta software, so there may be a few bugs and rough edges along the way. Feedback and suggestions from other operators will play an important role in helping the software continue to grow.

This video is simply an introduction to ParkWatch, why I decided to create it, and the ideas behind my summer development project.

Hunting new portable references has never been so easy—and this is only the beginning.

#ParkWatch, #POTA, #HamRadio

snippet.title: GMRS Radio for Beginners: How It Works & How to Get Started
snippet.description:
#gmrs #EmergencyCommunications #preparedness 

New to GMRS radio and not sure where to start? This beginner’s guide breaks down the basics of GMRS radio, including GMRS vs FRS, simplex communication, repeaters, repeater offsets, CHIRP programming, CTCSS/DCS tones, and how to program a GMRS repeater into your radio.

If you’re getting into emergency communications, preparedness, off-grid communication, or just want better range than standard walkie-talkies, GMRS is one of the easiest places to start.

In this video, we cover:
• What GMRS radio is
• GMRS licensing basics
• GMRS vs FRS radios
• Simplex radio-to-radio communication
• How GMRS repeaters work
• GMRS repeater input and output frequencies
• Understanding the +5 MHz repeater offset
• Live simplex vs repeater demonstrations
• How to use CHIRP programming software
• GMRS channels and repeater channels
• CTCSS and DCS repeater tones
• How to manually program a GMRS repeater
• GMRS handheld radios vs 50-watt base/mobile radios

If you’re building a family emergency communication plan, GMRS gives you a relatively simple way to communicate locally while also giving you access to repeaters that can dramatically extend your range.

snippet.description:
Free Video Course - The Top 5 Beginner Ham Radio Frustrations (and How To Overcome Them): https://hamradiolaunchpad.com/free
